# mmx-pri-1 — a Dwarf Priest on depth 1, stopped alive at character level 2

**Seed 17. Class Priest (given). Race drawn: Dwarf.** 149 asks, 984 keypresses,
9952 game turns. Maximum depth 1. Character level 2 (28 of the 30 experience a
Dwarf needs for level 3). Alive: stopped, saved, 24/24 hit points, 4/4 spell
points, AC 9, 8 gold, 18 flasks of oil. No down staircase found.

This is the first Priest in this repository and the first Dwarf, so most of
what is below is the class's own mechanics rather than a result.

## What the character was

A Dwarf Priest is the best-bodied Priest the game can make and the worst-armed:

- **Hit points.** Level 1 = 13 (the Dwarf's 11 hit die plus the Priest's 2) plus
  1 from constitution = 14. Level 2 = 24. The Dwarf's constitution modifier is
  +3 (race +2, class +1), which puts the CON stat at 19, and
  `adj_con_mhp[19] = 175` — **+1.75 hit points a level**, the best a Priest can
  have. A Mage or a Rogue would be under zero.
- **One blow a turn, always.** `calc_blows()` divides `adj_str_blow[STR]` by
  `max(weapon weight, class min-weight)`, and a Priest's min-weight is 35 and
  its strength-multiplier is 3, so the index is 0 for every weapon and the
  blow table gives exactly 100 energy a blow: **1.0 blows per turn whatever I
  hold**. Melee is not a fallback for this class, it is a rounding error.
- **The Mace is 2d4, not 1d1.** The birth sheet said "Melee 1d1,+2"; the
  equipment screen said "a Mace (2d4)". The birth sheet is the wrong place to
  read damage from.
- **Thrown oil is the attack.** Throw skill 35 (Dwarf 0 + Priest 35). A flask
  of oil has to-hit 35 **minus the distance to the target**, so at one tile it
  is 34 and it beats the AC 24 of a small kobold about 56% of the time, and
  even AC 36 (Grip, Fang, the large white snake) about 36%. The distance
  penalty is the thing to manage, not the number.
- **BLESS_WEAPON and ZERO_FAIL.** The mace is blessed (+2 to-hit). The spells
  still fail: the spell list's Fail column reads **5% for the level-1
  prayers** and 9% for Bless. `ZERO_FAIL` only means the failure rate is not
  floored at 5% for everyone else; the priest's own floor is `adj_mag_fail`
  for WIS 18, which is 5. A priest is not failure-free in this build.
- **The priest learns prayers at random.** At level 2 I was given two of the
  three learnable level-1 prayers and I got Minor Healing and Bless, which
  was luck: Detect Evil and Call Light were equally likely.

## What the shopping was, and what it bought

92 gold, and the whole question was how to spend it.

| bought | price | why |
|---|---|---|
| Soft Leather Armour | 84 | +8 AC, and it replaces the Robes, so AC 3 → AC 9 |
| 2 flasks of oil | 6 | the attack |

- **Gear is not priced from `object.txt`.** A Soft Leather Armour has
  `cost:20` in object.txt and the Armoury asks **84**, because gear is priced
  by power (`object_value_real`). I nearly planned the whole shopping list
  from the data file and it would have been wrong.
- **AC is the thing a fragile Priest is short of.** At 14 hit points a
  depth-1 monster with to-hit 12 hits me on 95% of turns at AC 3 and on 53%
  at AC 9. With a 10-damage soldier on depth 2, AC is what decides whether
  a mistake costs a potion or the run.
- **The flasks of oil are capped by weight, not gold.** A flask weighs 2 lb
  and STR 18 allows 119.9 lb, so more than about forty flasks is
  overweight. I bought 18 and found more on the level; I should have
  understood the cap earlier.
- **The other 16 gold went into a treasure vein.** A '*' on the map is a
  vein with treasure and a Dwarf can dig quartz: SKILL_DIGGING = race 40 +
  `adj_str_dig[STR 18]` 9 + `weapon_weight / 10` 12 = **61**, so quartz is
  82 of 1200 (6.8% an attempt), magma 204 (17%), granite 21 (1.75%). One 'T'
  plus a direction digs **and repeats by itself until the wall is gone** —
  one ask, a hundred attempts. The vein gave **90 gold in three attempts**.

## The fight with the mice, which is the part I would take back

A giant white mouse has 2 hit points, AC 4, 1d2 of damage and the MULTIPLY
flag, and one of them became eight in about fifteen turns. On a one-wide
corridor only the mouse in front of me could reach me, and **my blow comes
first in the turn**, so a mouse I kill never bites me: the first four cost me
nothing at all.

Then I went the wrong way. I walked a 38-digit route west along the corridor
and the mice behind me bit me every turn: **22 hit points in one ask**. The
lesson is arithmetic, not courage: *a breeding monster on the level is a tax
of one to two hit points on every ask, and a run with 50 asks left and 24 hit
points cannot pay it.* A player who meets a mouse nest on a fresh level
should either kill the lot in the corridor where only one can reach them, or
leave the level, and should not try to walk 38 tiles with them at its back.

I lost the rest of the run to that: about 30 asks and 30 hit points, and no
down staircase.

## The other things I got wrong

- **I read the wrong scroll.** The pack letters move when items are used up:
  after I drank both Potions of Cure Serious Wounds the two scrolls each
  moved down one letter, and 'f' was the Scroll of Word of Recall when I
  meant the Scroll of Phase Door. Read the letter off the screen of the
  prompt, every time — the quaff prompt, the read prompt and the wear list
  each print their own letters, and they are not the same list.
- **The flavour name does not identify a kind.** I worked out that the
  brown potion was the eighth potion in object.txt, which is Cure Light
  Wounds, and I said so in my notebook. `flavor_assign()` in
  `src/obj-util.c` hands the flavours out at random (`choice =
  randint0(flavor_count)`), so the index means nothing. The brown potion was
  a **Potion of Speed**. The way to identify an unknown potion for nothing is
  the Alchemist's 'd' (sell): `do_cmd_sell()` learns the runes before the
  item changes hands, and with selling off you get 0 gold and keep the
  knowledge.
- **The keypad.** 7 8 9 / 4 5 6 / 1 2 3: '3' is down-**right** and '4' is
  **left**. I got both wrong once each and lost asks.
- **An aim at an unknown tile is not a walk.** '*p' + twelve digits east
  moved me one tile **west**. Aim only at a tile the map has already drawn,
  and use a digit string otherwise.
- **A digit string can lose a digit.** Forty-one digits moved me forty
  tiles. Check the position after every long route, not the message line.

## What the screens and the source gave me that the manuals do not

- **The torch lights three tiles.** `Light 2` and
  `cave-view.c calc_lighting()`'s `radius = ABS(cur_light) - 1` gives a
  3x3 view. The map panel carries more than the light, because
  `become_viewable()` marks the walls next to a lit square as seen, so a
  corridor reveals a strip as I walk it.
- **The M map is the only way to look at the whole remembered level**, and
  its priority array keeps a remembered staircase's cell, so a '>' cannot be
  hidden by the 2.5:1 scaling. Two of my three M-map checks found nothing,
  which is how I knew my remembered area was about sixty squares of 13,068.
- **A level change ends in a -more-**, and so does a message, and **a screen
  that is a menu eats the first key of the next ask**: the M view, the store
  and the equipment list all took a key from me.
- **The Word of Recall's timer is 15 to 34 player actions** and it fires
  wherever you are when it does — it took me to the town in the middle of a
  corridor walk, with "There is a wall in the way!" as the message. It did
  **not** heal me; the heal in `minimaxflash-1-again`'s report was a rest in
  the town.
- **The rest prompt is pre-filled with '& '** and '&' alone rests as needed,
  so 'R' and Enter is the one-ask rest. In the town it healed about four hit
  points in sixteen actions and was interrupted by a boil-covered wretch.
- **The store's keys**: 'p' then the item's letter then the quantity then
  Enter then any other key buys in one ask; pressing an item's letter
  *without* 'p' opens that item's own menu (l Examine / p Buy / o Buy one);
  ESC leaves.
- **Walking into a wall does not dig** — "There is a wall in the way!" — the
  digging command is 'T' plus a direction.
- **Chest traps are in `chest_trap.txt`**: a poison gas at level 1, a poison
  needle (1d4 and a permanent STR or CON loss) at levels 2 and 3, summoning
  runes at level 15 and a 5d8 exploding device at level 25. I left the chest
  on depth 1 alone for that reason and would again: a poison gas is 10 to 30
  turns of poison, which at 24 hit points is a death sentence dressed as a
  potion.

## The leads, and what would settle them

1. **A down staircase is on a square with three adjacent walls** — a corridor
   end — and there are three or four of them per level, at least 16 tiles
   apart. I checked every dead end I found on depth 1 and none of them had
   one, which is the expected result of covering sixty squares of 13,068.
   *What would settle it:* a run that walks only corridor ends and reports
   where the '>' actually appears, and how many dead ends there are per
   down staircase — if most dead ends are not staircases, the "look for the
   three walls" heuristic is weaker than it sounds.
2. **The town-and-depth-1 shuttle is worth testing properly.** Every descent
   from the town builds a *new* depth 1 with new monsters, and on the two
   fresh levels I saw the monsters were 1-experience mice while the depth-1
   table promises small kobolds at 5 and soldier ants at 3. *What would
   settle it:* a run that descends, kills what is beside the staircase and
   comes back up, counting the kills per ask and the experience per kill, and
   says where the good monsters actually are.
3. **The mouse tax is measurable.** One 38-digit walk cost 22 hit points.
   *What would settle it:* the same walk taken with the monster killed
   behind you before each step, which I believe would cost almost nothing.
4. **Whether a Priest's spell failure is ever zero.** The list says 5%.
   *What would settle it:* cast a level-1 prayer twenty times and count.

## What I would do differently

- Buy the Soft Leather Armour and go straight back down, and leave the
  mice alone as soon as there are more than three of them.
- Learn the trade of the town before the dungeon: the armour, the oil, and
  the two prayers are worth more than the first hour of exploration.
- Never believe a number I have read off a data file when the screen prints
  the number too (the flavour index, the mace's damage, the armour's price).
- Dig on the way past, always: one ask bought 90 gold and it is the only
  income a Priest has that does not depend on the dice.
